extracted.intended_audience: attorneys practicing before the USPTO, OED staff, and counsel involved in disciplinary/reciprocal proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Final order applying 37 C.F.R. §11.24 to impose reciprocal exclusion from practice before the USPTO based on state-court disbarment, and describing the required service, response timeline, standards for determination, and notice/ publication of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Reciprocal Discipline / Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion ordered for violation of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. §10.23(c)(5)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order relies on the state-court disbarment based on uncontested evidence of professional misconduct (conversion of settlement funds held in escrow totaling approximately $244,000) and the respondent's criminal conviction (pled guilty to grand larceny in the third degree, Penal Law §155.35). The exclusion is the reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the Appellate Division, First Department, New York.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutory and regulatory provisions as the legal basis for imposing reciprocal discipline, publishing notice, and notifying other agencies/courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice — Mailing to Last Known Address
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order must be mailed by certified mail to the respondent at the last address known to the OED Director and must inform the respondent of the Complaint and opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order in this matter was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. given) to the last known address and informed respondent he had forty days to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline on specified grounds (per 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by Publication When Mail is Undeliverable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mailed Notice and Order is returned as undeliverable, service may be effected by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.35(b) in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the mailed notice was returned with explanation that respondent had moved and his mail was not forwardable; the OED served respondent by publication in the Official Gazette (dates provided). The publication must provide directions on how to request copies of the Notice and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response Period and Consequence of Non-Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is afforded a forty-day period to file a response to the Notice and Order; failure to request copies or file a response within that period can lead to a default determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published notice informed respondent how to request a copy; it has been more than forty days since the second publication and respondent did not request documents or file a response — resulting in the determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and that exclusion is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for Determination under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the respondent fails to respond, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Analysis states: 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that: (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and (2) the exclusion of Respondent from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.' This describes the legal standard and consequence for non-response in reciprocal-discipline proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of Misconduct That Warrants Discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of client/settlement funds held in escrow to personal use and criminal conviction for grand larceny constitute professional misconduct warranting disbarment/reciprocal exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice summarizes the state-court findings: conversion of settlement funds (~$244,000); guilty plea to grand larceny in the third degree; sentence (three year conditional discharge and 200 hours community service). These factual findings support the ethical violation cited (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies / Relief Ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may order exclusion from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO and direct further actions by the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies relief: (A) respondent is excluded from practice before the USPTO effective the date of the Final Order; (B) direct OED Director to publish the Notice in the Official Gazette; (C) give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59 to state disciplinary agencies, courts where respondent is admitted, and the public; and (D) other relief as nature requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Content and Public Posting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Exclusion must be published in the Official Gazette and disciplinary decisions must be posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document includes a model 'NOTICE OF EXCLUSION' containing required elements: respondent identity, statement that respondent is not a registered patent practitioner and not authorized to practice patent law before the USPTO, citation of the violated regulation (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6) via §10.23(c)(5)(i)), summary of state-court findings (misconduct and criminal conviction), statutory/regulatory authority for the action, and reference to where decisions are posted (http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Notice to Other Jurisdictions and Public (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must notify disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and the public of the discipline and reasons therefor pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly directs the OED Director to give such notice, ensuring other jurisdictions and the public are informed of the disciplinary action and underlying reasons.
